title: feat(jetbrains): the board's Done column renders only its newest 200 cards (land the human's BoardDoneCap work)
description:
Land the human's JetBrains Done-column cap. The human wrote it in their own Claude session and decided on 2026-11-05 (about 07:20Z) that it ships with the next work→main merge. The bytes are finished but not on the work branch. They are in commit 1f1913db, kept at refs/backup/governor/control-1f1913db and also saved as /mnt/d/moe-scratch/governor/control-1f1913db-20261105T070403Z.patch.

WHAT IT DOES. Every DONE task is a Swing card (a handful of components and listeners) rebuilt on each board change, so a long-lived board rebuilds hundreds of them. BoardDoneCap.visible(tasks, DONE_COLUMN_CAP = 200) keeps the newest 200 DONE cards, ordered by updatedAt, else completedAt, else createdAt, then the higher order. A missing stamp counts as oldest. The kept cards stay in the column's own order. The column header counts the hidden cards too, and a footer line names them: "+ {0} older done tasks not shown — Clear Done archives them" (MoeBundle moe.column.doneHidden). Task gains createdAt, updatedAt and completedAt, which MoeJson parses at both task parse sites. The Done column's render fingerprint includes the hidden count.

TAKE EXACTLY THESE 8 PATHS from that commit, and nothing else:
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BoardDoneCap.kt (new)
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MoeToolWindowPanel.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/board/TaskColumn.kt
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties
- moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BoardDoneCapTest.kt (new)
- moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJsonTest.kt
Write them into the task worktree with read-only git, keeping the bytes exact: `git show refs/backup/governor/control-1f1913db:<path> > <path>`. Since 1f1913db, no commit on the target touches moe-jetbrains. Never take the commit's other two paths. scripts/moe-agent.sh there is a corrupted leftover (NUL bytes, and it reverts e53f5a5c), and 2026-10-24-ai-code-quality-and-context.md only gains a stray blank line.

Keep the human's design and bytes. Change something only where the build, ./gradlew test or QA requires it, and name each change and its reason in the step note. VS Code parity is not part of this row.

CONTROL CHECKOUT. D:/projexts/moes holds the same 8 files as byte-identical uncommitted edits, which the governor STAGED so that this row's landing fast-forwards control over them unchanged. Work only in the task worktree, and never touch the control checkout. If you had to change any of the 8 files, say so in the completion note, so the governor can clear that path's staged copy before the control follow.
definitionOfDone: Exactly the 8 listed moe-jetbrains paths change against the target, with the bytes of refs/backup/governor/control-1f1913db except where a fix is named in a step note. No other path changes.

With more than 200 DONE tasks, the Done column renders only the newest 200 (updatedAt, else completedAt, else createdAt, then the higher order) in the column's own order. The header count includes the hidden tasks, and the footer line names how many are hidden. With 200 or fewer, nothing is hidden and there is no footer. BoardDoneCapTest covers both cases.
MoeJson parses createdAt, updatedAt and completedAt at both task parse sites, and an absent field parses to null. MoeJsonTest covers it.
./gradlew test and ./gradlew buildPlugin pass in moe-jetbrains for the task worktree's tree, with the jetbrains-gradle lease held for the run.

Theoretical notes, not fixed (they are the human's design):
(a) Stamps compare as strings. That holds because the daemon writes UTC toISOString with millis; a stamp without millis would sort as newer than a millis stamp from the same second.
(b) visible() keys the kept set on id, so duplicate ids could miscount. Daemon ids are unique.
(c) DONE_COLUMN_CAP = 200 is pinned only by reference, since the tests use cap 2 and a 201 mutant would survive. The Swing header and footer have no headless test.
(d) The outer board fingerprint omits updatedAt, so a re-sort driven only by an updatedAt change waits for the next board change.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) `git show R:<path> > <path>`, as the description spells it. Rejected because it is a shell write into the tree, which the global rail forbids. In worktree mode the rail's stated consequence (a contested HELD path) cannot happen (scripts/CLAUDE.md, 'Attribution in W'). Edit/Write still satisfies both the rail and the description, and checkRefs[0] mechanically proves byte identity, which is the description's real requirement.
(2) `git cherry-pick 1f1913db` or `git checkout R -- <paths>`. Rejected: the cherry-pick would bring in the corrupt scripts/moe-agent.sh and the stray .md line, and the checkout is a git write that also stages.

The gate therefore runs in a /mnt/d/moe-scratch snapshot, matching the rail that npm runs only in a snapshot outside the repo.
